 / German Sales Call Playbook
      

      
Germany Sales Pillar Guide

      
German B2B Sales Call Scripts: Cold Calling & Discovery Frameworks for Enterprise & Mittelstand

      

        
Updated: August 2026

        
21 min read

        
Includes 5 Industry Playbooks

      

    

    

      

        Conducting cold calls and technical discovery in Germany requires strict adherence to legal compliance (UWG § 7, mutmaßliche Einwilligung), structured gatekeeper protocols (Vorzimmer), and fact-driven qualification. This comprehensive pillar guide delivers tested German cold call scripts, gatekeeper bypass techniques, and discovery frameworks across 5 key B2B sectors: SaaS, Pharma, Energy, Higher Education, and Insurance.
      

      

        
Table of Contents

        

          

1. Legal & Cultural Framework for German Cold Calls (UWG § 7)

          

2. The Vorzimmer Protocol: Navigating German Gatekeepers

          

3. Industry Playbook 1: B2B SaaS & Cloud Infrastructure

          

4. Industry Playbook 2: Pharma & Life Sciences

          

5. Industry Playbook 3: Energy & Utilities

          

6. Industry Playbook 4: Higher Education & EdTech

          

7. Industry Playbook 5: Insurance & InsurTech

          

8. Master Objection Handling in German Calls

        

      

      
1. Legal & Cultural Framework for German Cold Calls (UWG § 7)

      

        B2B cold calling in Germany is regulated under § 7 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 of the Law Against Unfair Competition (Gesetz gegen den unlauteren Wettbewerb - UWG). Calling a business entity is legally permissible only under the doctrine of 
"mutmaßliche Einwilligung"
 (presumed consent).
      

      

        
Criteria for Presumed Consent (Mutmaßliche Einwilligung)

        

          

Direct Subject Matter Nexus:
 The offered solution must address a specific, objectively demonstrable operational problem relevant to the prospect's exact job function and current industry requirements.

          

B2B Only:
 Calls must target commercial business entities, not consumers or private telephone lines.

          

Immediate Identification:
 The caller must state their name, legal company identity, and the precise business purpose immediately upon connection.

        

      

      
Cultural Dynamics of German Phone Discovery

      

        

Tone:
 Calm, analytical, unhurried, and precise. Avoid enthusiastic pitch-cadence typical of North American outbound.

        

Formality:
 Always use formal "Sie" with exact academic titles (e.g., 
Herr Dr. Becker
). Never use first names unless explicitly invited.

        

Pacing:
 Do not interrupt. Allow the prospect to finish their thoughts completely before responding.

      

      
2. The Vorzimmer Protocol: Navigating German Gatekeepers

      

        Executive assistants and receptionists (
Vorzimmer / Assistenz der Geschäftsführung
) in German enterprises and Mittelstand companies are trained gatekeepers. Aggressive or evasive tactics trigger immediate dismissal. Treat the gatekeeper as an internal partner.
      

      

        

          
Gatekeeper Script: Direct & Transparent

          
Formal German

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag, mein Name ist [Vorname Nachname] von [Unternehmen]. Ich benötige bitte Ihre Unterstützung: Wer in Ihrem Haus leitet aktuell die strategische Optimierung der [z. B. Cloud-Infrastruktur / DSGVO-Prozesse]?"

Assistenz: "Worum genau geht es denn?"

SDR: "Es geht um einen kurzen Erfahrungsaustausch zu den neuen DACH-Vorgaben für [Thema]. Wir haben dazu Benchmark-Daten aus der Branche aufbereitet und möchten prüfen, ob dies für Frau Dr. [Nachname] relevant ist. Können Sie mich direkt mit ihrem Büro verbinden?"

        

          
Key Mechanism:
 Transparently states topic, respects gatekeeper authority, uses industry context rather than generic sales jargon.
        

      

      
3. Industry Playbook 1: B2B SaaS & Cloud Infrastructure

      

        German engineering and product leaders are skeptical of bloated feature claims. Focus on API latency, infrastructure cost efficiency (de-bloating), and data sovereignty (Frankfurt AWS/GCP regions, ISO 27001).
      

      

        

          
B2B SaaS Cold Call Script

          
Engineering & VP Product

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag Herr [Nachname], mein Name ist [Ihr Name] von [Ihr Unternehmen]. Ich rufe Sie direkt an, weil Sie bei [Unternehmen] für die Software-Architektur verantwortlich sind. Haben Sie eine Minute?"

Prospect: "Ja, worum geht es ganz konkret?"

SDR: "Wir stellen bei wachsenden B2B-SaaS-Unternehmen in Deutschland fest, dass unoptimierte LLM-Tokens und redundante Datenbankabfragen die monatlichen Cloud-Rechnungen um 20% bis 35% aufblähen und die API-Latenz belasten.

Wir haben für Unternehmen wie [Kunde] ein 48-Stunden-Audit-Verfahren entwickelt, das diese Engpässe identifiziert und die Infrastrukturkosten um durchschnittlich 4.000 € pro Monat senkt. 

Wäre es für Sie denkbar, nächste Woche kurz 10 Minuten in Ihren Kalender zu schauen, um zu prüfen, ob ähnliche Potenziale bei Ihrer Architektur existieren?"

        

          
Discovery Focus:
 Identify database indexing overhead, token usage tracking, and serverless compute over-provisioning.
        

      

      
4. Industry Playbook 2: Pharma & Life Sciences

      

        Pharma organizations operate under BfArM and EMA compliance mandates, stringent GxP validations, and multi-layered clinical review boards.
      

      

        

          
Pharma Discovery Script

          
Clinical Operations & Compliance

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag Frau Dr. [Nachname], mein Name ist [Ihr Name] von [Ihr Unternehmen]. Ich melde mich bezüglich der Dokumentations-Workflows im Bereich klinische Studien und Datenvalidierung.

Bei der Zusammenarbeit mit pharmazeutischen Herstellern in der DACH-Region sehen wir häufig, dass die Vorbereitung von Einreichungen unter GxP-Richtlinien bis zu 40% mehr manuelle Arbeitszeit bindet als notwendig.

Wir unterstützen Qualitäts- und Regulatory-Affairs-Teams dabei, diesen Prozess durch standardisierte Validierungs-Pipelines vollkommen audit-sicher um 60% zu beschleunigen.

Hätten Sie am Donnerstag um 14:00 Uhr Zeit für einen 15-minütigen Fachaustausch?"

        

          
Discovery Focus:
 Audit readiness, GxP compliance documentation, BfArM regulatory bottlenecks.
        

      

      
5. Industry Playbook 3: Energy & Utilities (Stadtwerke)

      

        Municipal utilities (Stadtwerke) and energy providers prioritize grid stability, EnWG compliance, ESG transparency, and integration with legacy ERP systems (SAP IS-U).
      

      

        

          
Energy & Utilities Script

          
Operations & Grid Management

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag Herr [Nachname], mein Name ist [Ihr Name] von [Ihr Unternehmen]. Ich rufe an bezüglich der Digitalisierung von Netzmessdaten und Verbrauchsabrechnungen.

Aktuell stehen viele Stadtwerke und regionale Versorger vor der Herausforderung, die Vorgaben zur Smart-Meter-Rollout-Dokumentation ohne hohe personelle Zusatzbelastung umzusetzen.

Wir ermöglichen Stadtwerken eine automatisierte Schnittstellenanbindung an bestehende ERP-Systeme, wodurch manuelle Übertragungsfehler vollständig eliminiert werden.

Wäre es für Sie von Interesse, die Methodik in einem kurzen 15-minütigen Termin für Ihr Versorgungsgebiet durchzugehen?"

        

          
Discovery Focus:
 Smart-metering compliance, SAP integration friction, manual reconciliation elimination.
        

      

      
6. Industry Playbook 4: Higher Education & EdTech

      

        Universities and educational institutions in DACH face strict public procurement cycles, DSGVO privacy barriers, and distributed faculty decision-making.
      

      

        

          
Higher Education Script

          
Administration & Dean of Studies

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag Frau Professor [Nachname], mein Name ist [Ihr Name] von [Ihr Unternehmen]. Ich kontaktiere Sie zur Verwaltung digitaler Prüfungsprozesse und Studierenden-Workflows.

Viele Hochschulverwaltungen in Deutschland kämpfen aktuell mit fragmentierten Einzellösungen, die weder vollständig barrierefrei noch DSGVO-konform integriert sind.

Unsere Plattform zentralisiert diese Prozesse unter Einhaltung aller Vorgaben der Kultusministerkonferenz und entlastet die Lehrstuhlassistenzen um mehrere Stunden wöchentlich.

Darf ich Ihnen eine kurze Fallstudie dazu per E-Mail senden und nächste Woche dazu kurz Rücksprache halten?"

        

          
Discovery Focus:
 Compliance with German state education mandates, faculty workload, student privacy.
        

      

      
7. Industry Playbook 5: Insurance & InsurTech

      

        Insurance providers (Versicherungen & Assekuranz) require BaFin compliance, actuarial risk rigor, and seamless integration with legacy core insurance platforms.
      

      

        

          
Insurance Discovery Script

          
Claims & Actuarial Operations

        

        
SDR: "Guten Tag Herr Dr. [Nachname], mein Name ist [Ihr Name] von [Ihr Unternehmen]. Ich wende mich an Sie im Zusammenhang mit der automatisierten Schadenregulierung und Risikobewertung.

Versicherer stehen vor der Herausforderung, Standard-Schadensfälle innerhalb von Minuten statt Tagen abzuwickeln, ohne die BaFin-Prüfstandards oder versicherungsmathematische Sorgfalt zu verletzen.

Mit unserer Lösung konnten Assekuranzen die Dunkelverarbeitungsquote um 28% steigern und die Bearbeitungszeit pro Fall von 4 Tagen auf unter 2 Stunden senken.

Lassen Sie uns nächste Woche in einem kurzen 15-minütigen Fachgespräch prüfen, wie sich diese Kennzahlen auf Ihre Schadenquote übertragen lassen."

        

          
Discovery Focus:
 BaFin regulatory compliance, Dunkelverarbeitung (straight-through processing), claims cycle compression.
        

      

      
8. Master Objection Handling in German Calls

      
      

        
Objection 1: "Wir haben bereits eine bestehende Lösung im Einsatz."

        

Response Script:
 
"Das habe ich bei einem Unternehmen Ihrer Größe vorausgesetzt, Herr [Nachname]. Es geht uns auch nicht darum, Ihre bestehenden Systeme abzulösen, sondern zu prüfen, ob es Schnittstellen oder Optimierungspotenziale gibt, die Ihre aktuelle Lösung ergänzen. Wie zufrieden sind Sie aktuell mit [konkreter Engpass, z. B. der monatlichen Abrechnungsgeschwindigkeit]?"

      

      

        
Objection 2: "Schicken Sie mir einfach Unterlagen zu."

        

Response Script:
 
"Sehr gerne mache ich das, Frau [Nachname]. Damit ich Ihnen nicht 30 Seiten allgemeines Marketing-Material zusende, sondern genau das, was für Ihre Abteilung relevant ist: Welcher Bereich ist bei Ihnen aktuell der wichtigste Fokus – [Bereich A] oder [Bereich B]?"

      

      

        
Objection 3: "Ich habe jetzt absolut keine Zeit."

        

Response Script:
 
"Verstehe ich vollkommen, Herr [Nachname]. Wann passt es Ihnen im Laufe der Woche besser für ein kurzes, 5-minütiges Gespräch – Donnerstagvormittag oder Freitagnachmittag?"

      

      

        
Objection 4: "Kein Interesse."

        

Response Script:
 
"Vielen Dank für Ihre Offenheit. Liegt es am aktuellen Zeitpunkt oder haben Sie das Thema für dieses Geschäftsjahr intern bereits abgeschlossen gelöst?"

## https://zerohypelab.com/manifesto/

Manifesto — No Fluff. No Hype. Just What Works. · Zero Hype

Zero Hype

      

        

Manifesto

        

Guides

        

Newsletter

        

X

        

About

      

    

    

      
manifesto

      
No fluff.
No hype.
Just what
works.

      
most b2b marketing fails at the strategy layer, not the execution layer. here's what we believe — and why diagnosis always comes before execution.

    

  

  

    

      
the pattern

      
you know this story.

      
someone has a pipeline problem. they hire an agency, a consultant, or a head of growth. six weeks later there's a strategy document. twelve weeks later there's a content calendar and an automation sequence. six months later the pipeline problem is still there but now it has a narrative and a color palette.

      
this is not a cynicism exercise. this is just what happens when activity gets mistaken for diagnosis.

      
"activity is not the same thing as diagnosis."

    

    

    

      
what we believe

      
strategy fails before execution does.

      
most b2b marketing fails at the strategy layer, not the execution layer. the campaigns don't underperform because of bad copy or wrong send times. they underperform because the assumptions underneath them were never tested.

      
wrong icp. vague goal. channel picked for comfort, not fit. message that sounds like every other message in the inbox.

      
ai didn't create this problem. ai made it faster and cheaper to produce more of it. we've reviewed over 200 cold outreach sequences that weren't working. the failure reasons repeat. they almost always do.

      
"personalization at scale" is not a solution to broken positioning. it's broken positioning, delivered personally, at volume, with a first name in the subject line.

    

    

    

      
what we do

      
forensic diagnosis.
no padding.

      
we audit b2b marketing that isn't working and tell you exactly why it isn't working. not a report with 47 recommendations. not a retainer to implement the strategy we just told you was wrong.

      
a specific, honest answer to the question: what is actually broken here and what would it take to fix it.

      
cold outreach that fails, fails for reasons. campaigns that underperform, underperform for reasons. most companies never find out what those reasons are because they're already running the next campaign.

      
"we find the reasons."

    

    

    

      
what we don't do

      
we're not an agency.

      
we don't build you a content machine. we don't manage your linkedin. we don't run your ads. we don't optimize your automation sequences.

      
we don't compete with agencies that sell volume. we don't compete with consultants who need a 6-month retainer to tell you something you could have figured out in week two.

      
one thing: diagnosis. the name is the constraint. if we can't say it plainly, we don't say it.

    

    

      
start with
a free tool.

      
paste your cold email. run your campaign through the predictor. see what's actually broken before you pay anything.

      
cold email roaster — free →

## https://zerohypelab.com/method/

How We Score. The Whole Method · Zero Hype

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  
  

  

  

  

  

  

  

  
Skip to main content

Wall of Scores

        

Guides

        

Newsletter

        

About

      

    

    

      
method

      
How we score.
All of it.

      
no black box. here's exactly what we measure when we score a cold email or a campaign, the language that drags a score down, and the work we will never sell you. if you'd rather game the test than fix the email, that's your call. the prospect will notice either way.

    

  

  

    

      
the principle

      
a score you can't see
is just an opinion.

      
every free tool here gives you a number. a Hype Score on a cold email. a failure risk on a campaign. a number is easy to dismiss if you don't know how it was reached, so here is how it's reached. the whole thing. no login required to read it, no login required to run it.

      
"if we can't show you the math, we haven't earned the score."

    

    

    

      
inside the cold email roaster

      
six checks.
that's the engine.

      
paste a cold email and it runs through six checks. none of them are secret. none of them need AI to explain. each one maps to a reason real B2B emails get ignored.

      

        
1. Jargon density

        
how much of the email is filler language that means nothing to the reader. the more recognized B2B jargon it finds, the higher the Hype Score climbs. a sample of what gets flagged is below.

      

      

        
2. The opener

        
the first line. whether it's about them or about you. "I hope this email finds you well" and "I'm reaching out because" are openers that announce a template.

      

      

        
3. Length

        
how long it is versus how long a cold email should be before a stranger stops reading. most failing emails are too long, not too short.

      

      

        
4. The I / you ratio

        
how many times the email talks about your company versus the reader's problem. emails that lead with "we" and "our platform" score worse than emails that lead with the reader.

      

      

        
5. CTA quality

        
what you actually ask for. "a quick 15-minute call to explore synergies" is a worse ask than a specific, low-friction next step. vague asks get ignored.

      

      

        
6. Personalization

        
whether there's a real, specific reason this email was sent to this person, or whether their first name was dropped into a template and called personalization.

      

    

    

    

      
the language that costs you

      
the whole list.
all 71.

      
not a sample. this is every phrase the roaster flags, in full. if your cold email leans on these, the reader has seen them a hundred times this week. nothing here is a secret, so here's all of it.

      

        
hope this email finds you well

        
hope this finds you well

i hope you're doing well

reading the score

      
lower is better.

      
the Hype Score runs 0 to 100. zero means a stranger could read it and not flinch. one hundred means it reads like it was generated to hit a quota. these are the exact six verdicts the roaster hands back.

      

0–10

Suspiciously human. Someone wrote this on purpose. Don't ruin it.

      

11–22

Mild jargon. The bones are solid, shower off the residue.

      

23–38

Classic SDR energy. Familiar, forgettable, lost in 47 identical inboxes.

      

39–58

LinkedIn DM cosplay. High cringe, low conversion.

      

59–78

Corporate word soup. A buzzword buffet with no main course.

      

79–100

Peak B2B BS. A collector's item. Don't send it to a living human.

    

    

    

      
the part most people hide

      
what we won't
sell you.

      
the offer is one thing: a written diagnosis of what's broken, and the fix. that's it. here's what is not on the menu, on purpose.

      

        
No retainer that bills for activity instead of outcomes.

        
we don't get paid more for sending you more. one diagnosis, one price.

      

      

        
No twelve-month contract.

        
nothing to lock into. you buy a thing, you get the thing.

      

      

        
No "book a call to discuss your needs."

        
the price is on the page. the deliverable is described on the page. async by default.

      

      

        
No deliverable you can't measure.

        
no "brand awareness" line items. if you can't tell whether it worked, we didn't sell it.

      

    

    

    

      
before you pay anything

      
you probably don't
need us yet.

      
run the free roaster first. if it scores you under 30, your email is fine. fix whatever it flagged and send it. come back when you've plateaued and the replies still aren't coming, because that's a positioning problem, and positioning is what we're actually for.

    

    

      
see the score
for yourself.

      
paste your cold email. no login, no email required. you'll get the number and the six checks behind it in about ten seconds.

      
run the free roaster →

Hiring a Marketing Consultant

      
A B2B marketing consultant costs $5k-15k/month. The first thing they do is diagnose your current state. Zero Hype does the diagnosis for $49-$99. The question is whether you need the execution that follows.

If you know what's broken but need someone to fix it for you, hire a consultant. If you're not sure what's broken — or you suspect you know but want an outside read before committing to $60k/year of retainer — start with Zero Hype. The audit pays for itself if it saves you from hiring the wrong person to fix the wrong problem.

The expensive part of hiring a consultant is onboarding them

    
Every consultant starts the same way: discovery calls, stakeholder interviews, reviewing your current assets, mapping your funnel. This takes 4-8 weeks. At $8k/month, you've spent $16k before a single recommendation lands.

    
Most of what they find in those first 8 weeks is what the Zero Hype audits surface in 48-72 hours. Wrong ICP assumptions. Messaging that talks about features instead of problems. A pipeline that looks active but is full of bad-fit prospects. Channel strategy that made sense in 2021 but doesn't now.

    
The difference is what happens next. A consultant stays and executes. Zero Hype gives you the diagnosis and you implement — or you hire someone specifically for execution once you know what to execute.

    

The best use of Zero Hype before a consultant hire:
 get the audit first, validate your diagnosis, then hire a consultant to solve a specific, confirmed problem. Not a vague "we need to fix our pipeline."

  

  

    
GET THE DIAGNOSIS
BEFORE THE RETAINER

    
$99 audit. 48-72 hour turnaround. Based on direct analysis of 100+ B2B campaigns in DACH and English-speaking markets.

    

      
Outreach Autopsy $99 →

      
Marketing Autopsy $49

    

  

  

    
Questions

    

      

        
Can Zero Hype replace a full-time marketing hire?

        
No. A full-time hire executes daily. Zero Hype diagnoses and advises. The Revenue Architecture ($4,500) goes further — 12 weeks of strategic work — but it's still async advisory, not embedded execution. If you need someone in the team building campaigns daily, hire for that specifically.

      

      

        
I've already hired a consultant but results are slow. Does Zero Hype help?

        
Possibly. The Marketing Autopsy ($49) can give you an independent read on whether the strategy your consultant is executing is sound. Sometimes the problem is execution. Sometimes it's the strategy. An outside diagnosis clarifies which.

      

      

        
Zero Hype is one person, right? Is that a problem?

        
The audits and diagnostics are based on direct B2B marketing experience across DACH and English-speaking markets. There's no team of junior analysts generalizing from a framework. The disadvantage is capacity — Zero Hype can't run your campaigns. The advantage is you get the honest read, not the polished deck.

      

      

        
What's the Monthly Autopsy compared to a consultant retainer?

        
The Monthly Autopsy ($300/month) reviews one campaign per month, rewrites the three weakest elements, and turns around in 48 hours. It's not a full retainer — no calls, no project management, no execution. It's the ongoing diagnostic layer for teams that execute themselves but want an outside eye on whether the strategy is drifting.

vs. Lavender

      
Lavender fixes how your email reads. Zero Hype diagnoses why your outreach is failing. One of these helps when the email is the problem. The other helps when the strategy is the problem.

    

  

  

    

      
Direct answer

      
If your cold emails have low open rates or generic replies, Lavender can help you write better sentences. If your pipeline is dry despite good writing, the problem is upstream — wrong ICP, bad positioning, wrong channel. That's what Zero Hype audits. Use both if needed. Use neither if your real issue is that you don't have a clear offer.

The problem Lavender can't fix

    
Lavender is genuinely useful for one thing: writing cold emails that don't sound like cold emails. It catches passive voice, flags overly long sentences, suggests more natural personalization. If your email reads like a template, Lavender helps.

    
But here's what we see consistently: B2B teams invest in better email writing while the real problem is that they're emailing the wrong people about the wrong thing. A beautifully written email to someone who has zero reason to care still gets ignored. Lavender can't fix your ICP. It can't fix your positioning. It can't tell you that cold email might not even be the right channel for your deal size.

    

Zero Hype works upstream.
 The Campaign Failure Predictor, the Outreach Autopsy, the Full Autopsy — they all start with the question Lavender never asks: should you even be doing this?

  

  

    
YOUR EMAIL ISN'T
THE PROBLEM

    
Before you optimize the writing, audit the strategy. Free tool, 60 seconds, honest score.

    

      
Run the Free Predictor

      
Get an Outreach Audit →

    

  

  

    
Questions

    

      

        
Should I use both Lavender and Zero Hype?

        
If your strategy is solid but your writing is weak, start with Lavender. If your strategy is broken, fix it first — otherwise you're optimizing something that's already pointing the wrong direction. Zero Hype first, then Lavender.

      

      

        
Zero Hype doesn't integrate with my email tool. Is that a problem?

        
Intentionally not. Zero Hype is an async diagnostic, not an inline assistant. The audit happens once, delivers a framework you apply across all your emails. The value is in the diagnosis, not the real-time suggestion.

      

      

        
My open rates are fine but reply rates are terrible. Which helps?

        
Reply rate is a strategy problem, not a writing problem. Good subject line, bad offer or wrong ICP. This is exactly what the Outreach Autopsy diagnoses: what's breaking between open and reply.

      

      

        
Is there a free way to test Zero Hype first?

        
Yes. The Campaign Failure Predictor is free — 10 questions, 60 seconds, tells you your failure risk score and the specific weak points in your outreach setup. No login, no email required.

Zero Hype
vs. Reply.io

      
Reply.io automates sequences at scale. Zero Hype diagnoses why your sequences aren't working. Automating a broken strategy just means more people ignore you faster.

    

  

  

    

      
Direct answer

      
Reply.io is infrastructure for outreach execution. If your sequences, targeting, and messaging are solid, it makes you faster. If they're broken, Reply.io scales the failure. Zero Hype audits what Reply.io assumes is already correct — your ICP, your positioning, your offer, your channel fit. Fix the strategy first. Then automate it.

Why automation makes bad strategy worse

    
The most common pattern we see: a team invests in Reply.io or Lemlist, builds a 7-step sequence, and sends 500 emails. 2% reply. They A/B test subject lines for 3 weeks. Still 2%. They upgrade the plan. Still 2%.

    
The problem isn't the tool. It's that the ICP is too broad, the email talks about the product instead of the prospect's problem, and the offer is unclear. Reply.io can't fix any of that. It just runs the sequence you gave it.

    

Zero Hype looks at what Reply.io assumes is already right.
 The Campaign Failure Predictor asks 10 questions that most teams skip before building a sequence. The Outreach Autopsy goes deeper: reviews your actual emails, scoring the opener, the ICP specificity, the CTA strength, the I/you ratio. Not to write better sentences. To find the strategic failure point.

  

  

    
BEFORE YOU SEND
500 MORE EMAILS

    
Score your campaign failure risk. Free, 60 seconds. Based on analysis of 100+ B2B campaigns.

    

      
Free Failure Predictor

      
Get Outreach Audited →

    

  

  

    
Questions

    

      

        
Can I use Reply.io and Zero Hype together?

        
Yes, and that's the right order. Get the audit first, fix the strategy and copy, then automate with Reply.io. Running audited sequences through automation is a much better bet than automating something broken.

      

      

        
My Reply.io sequences have good open rates but no replies. What's wrong?

        
Open rate is a subject line metric. Reply rate is a strategy metric. High opens, low replies means your targeting is decent but your email body, offer, or ICP is off. That's exactly what the Outreach Autopsy diagnoses.

      

      

        
Zero Hype is one-time. Reply.io is recurring. Which is more valuable?

        
Depends where the problem is. A one-time audit that fixes your positioning pays for itself in 1 good deal. Paying $200/month for automation on a broken strategy is a recurring loss. Start with diagnosis.

      

      

        
How long does a Zero Hype audit take?

        
The Campaign Failure Predictor takes 60 seconds. The Outreach Autopsy ($99) delivers in 48-72 hours — you send your emails and targeting context, we return a scored breakdown with specific rewrites for the weakest parts.
